techniques.name: Dreamer-CDP
techniques.capability_it_enables: Reconstruction-free model-based RL: a JEPA-style predictor over continuous, deterministic latent representations predicts the next abstract state instead of reconstructing pixels, matching Dreamer's performance on Crafter without any reconstruction objective.
techniques.code_url: https://github.com/fmi-basel/Dreamer-CDP (official repo; 'The official code is available at github.com/fmi-basel/Dreamer-CDP', tested on Linux, Python 3.11+)
techniques.verbatim_quote: Dreamer-CDP: Improving Reconstruction-free World Models Via Continuous Deterministic Representation Prediction

techniques.name: ProRL Agent (Rollout-as-a-Service)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Scalable multi-turn agentic RL training infrastructure that decouples the full rollout lifecycle (init/run/evaluate) from the GPU trainer via an HTTP rollout-as-a-service API, enabling rollout and training to run on separate machines with standardized sandbox environments.
techniques.code_url: https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/ProRL-Agent-Server (official NVIDIA repo; 'ProRL Agent is open-sourced and integrated as part of NVIDIA NeMo Gym', also github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym)
techniques.verbatim_quote: ProRL Agent: Rollout-as-a-Service for RL Training of Multi-Turn LLM Agents

techniques.name: DART (Disentangled Action Reasoning Tuning)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Resolves gradient interference between reasoning and tool-use in agentic RL by routing reasoning vs. tool-use tokens to disjoint LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone, so updates for the two capabilities never collide.
techniques.code_url: https://github.com/sheriyuo/DART (NOTE: described in results as an UNOFFICIAL/community implementation, not an author release; includes vocab fine-tuning, SFT and LoRA configs via ms-swift)
techniques.verbatim_quote: Reasoning and Tool-use Compete in Agentic RL: From Quantifying Interference to Disentangled Tuning

techniques.name: MolCrystalFlow
techniques.subfield: A: flow matching for molecular crystal structure prediction
techniques.capability_it_enables: Predicts molecular crystal structures by embedding molecules as rigid bodies and jointly learning the lattice matrix, molecular orientations and centroid positions on their native Riemannian manifolds via geodesic flow matching.
techniques.code_url: GitHub repository visible in search results: github.com/Liu-Group-UF/MolCrystalFlow ('Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction with Flow Matching').
techniques.verbatim_quote: The framework disentangles intramolecular complexity from intermolecular packing by embedding molecules as rigid bodies and jointly learning the lattice matrix, molecular orientations, and centroid positions.

techniques.name: EnFlow (Energy-Guided Flow Matching)
techniques.subfield: A: flow matching for molecular conformer generation / ground-state identification
techniques.capability_it_enables: Couples flow matching with an explicitly learned energy model via energy-guided sampling to produce high-fidelity molecular conformers and identify ground states in just 1-2 ODE steps.
techniques.code_url: Official code repository stated in search result: https://github.com/Rich-XGK/EnFlow.git
techniques.verbatim_quote: By incorporating energy-gradient guidance during sampling, this method steers trajectories toward lower-energy regions, substantially improving conformational fidelity, particularly in the few-step regime.

techniques.name: SymTorch
techniques.subfield: B: symbolic regression / symbolic distillation of neural networks
techniques.capability_it_enables: Wraps neural-network components (GNNs, PINNs, transformers), collects their input-output behavior, and replaces them with human-readable closed-form equations via PySR, enabling interpretability of trained models.
techniques.code_url: GitHub repo github.com/astroautomata/SymTorch plus ReadTheDocs documentation (symtorch.readthedocs.io) visible in search results.
techniques.verbatim_quote: SymTorch automates distillation by wrapping neural network components, collecting their input-output behavior, and approximating them with human-readable equations via PySR, while handling engineering challenges including GPU-CPU data transfer, input-output caching, model serialization, and seamless switching between neural and symbolic forward passes.

techniques.name: ShapPFN
techniques.capability_it_enables: Tabular foundation model that integrates Shapley value regression into its architecture, producing predictions and feature-importance explanations in a single forward pass, ~1000x faster than KernelSHAP (0.06s vs 610s).
techniques.code_url: WebSearch result block states code is available at GitHub: https://github.com/kunumi/ShapPFN
techniques.verbatim_quote: ShapPFN is a foundation model that integrates Shapley value regression directly into its architecture, producing both predictions and explanations in a single forward pass.

techniques.name: CANDI (Curated Test-Time Adaptation)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Test-time adaptation framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection under distribution shift; uses False Positive Mining and a plug-and-play Spatiotemporally-Aware Normality Adaptation module, improving AUROC up to 14% with fewer adaptation samples.
techniques.code_url: WebSearch result block: 'The code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/kimanki/CANDI'
techniques.verbatim_quote: CANDI introduces a False Positive Mining (FPM) strategy to curate adaptation samples based on anomaly scores and latent similarity, and incorporates a plug-and-play Spatiotemporally-Aware Normality Adaptation (SANA) module for structurally informed model updates.

techniques.name: ViT3 / ViTTT (Vision Test-Time Training)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Pure test-time-training architecture for vision achieving linear complexity and parallelizable computation; matches/outperforms Mamba and linear-attention variants across image classification, generation, object detection, and semantic segmentation. CVPR 2026 Oral.
techniques.code_url: Official GitHub repo surfaced in multiple result blocks: https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/ViTTT ('[CVPR 2026] [Oral] Official repository of Vision Test-Time Training'); search states 'code is available at https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/ViTTT'.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The Vision Test-Time Training (ViT3) model is a pure TTT architecture that achieves linear complexity and parallelizable computation.

techniques.name: VISION (Graph Few-Shot Learning via In-Context Learning)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Reframes graph few-shot node classification as a fine-tuning-free sequence reasoning (in-context learning) problem; conditions on the support set and generates class-aware query representations in a single forward pass, unifying unsupervised meta-learning with graph in-context learning.
techniques.code_url: Search summary states 'The public code is available, making it an open-source method'; abstract fragment quotes 'Our public code can be found' but the explicit GitHub URL was not surfaced in result blocks. Code availability asserted by authors; direct repo link not yet seen.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The method unifies unsupervised meta-learning with graph in-context learning, achieving efficient inference.

techniques.name: HOLOGRAPH: Active Causal Discovery via Sheaf-Theoretic Alignment of LLM Priors
techniques.capability_it_enables: LLM-guided active causal discovery that represents local causal beliefs as sheaf sections, handles hidden confounders via Algebraic Latent Projection, and uses Expected Free Energy to select maximally informative LLM queries (synthetic ER/SF and real Sachs benchmarks, 20-100 variables).
techniques.code_url: Search result states: 'Code and supplementary materials are available at: https://github.com/hyunjun1121/holograph' (repo also returned directly in GitHub search results).
techniques.verbatim_quote: HOLOGRAPH is a framework that formalizes LLM-guided causal discovery through sheaf theory--representing local causal beliefs as sections of a presheaf over variable subsets.

techniques.name: Large Causal Models (LCMs) for Temporal Causal Discovery
techniques.subfield: A: temporal causal discovery (pre-trained foundation model)
techniques.capability_it_enables: Pre-trained neural architectures (foundation-model style) for temporal causal discovery, trained at scale by combining diverse synthetic generators with realistic time-series datasets; released model weights enable amortized inference of temporal causal structure.
techniques.code_url: Search result states: 'The experiments and model weights are available at github.com/kougioulis/LCM-paper/.' HuggingFace papers page also listed.
techniques.verbatim_quote: The paper proposes Large Causal Models (LCMs), a class of pre-trained neural architectures specifically designed for temporal causal discovery, combining diverse synthetic generators with realistic time-series datasets.

techniques.name: CausalCompass: Robustness Benchmark for Time-Series Causal Discovery in Misspecified Scenarios
techniques.capability_it_enables: Extensible benchmark suite to assess robustness of time-series causal discovery (TSCD) methods across eight assumption-violation scenarios; finds deep-learning approaches strongest overall and exposes preprocessing dependence (e.g., NTS-NOTEARS needs standardization).
techniques.code_url: Search result states: 'The code and datasets are available at https://github.com/huiyang-yi/CausalCompass'.
techniques.verbatim_quote: CausalCompass is a flexible and extensible benchmark suite designed to assess the robustness of time-series causal discovery (TSCD) methods under violations of modeling assumptions.

techniques.name: Amortized Factor Inference Networks (AFINs) for Posterior Inference
techniques.capability_it_enables: Encode-merge-decode inference networks built on dimension-independent modules that map a model specification plus observations to variational posterior parameters; a single trained AFIN matches NUTS-level posterior accuracy while needing 2-4 orders of magnitude less test-time compute.
techniques.code_url: Search result states: 'Code is available at https://github.com/joohwanko/AFINs' (authors Joohwan Ko and Justin Domke).
techniques.verbatim_quote: Amortized Factor Inference Networks (AFINs) are a family of encode-merge-decode inference networks built on dimension-independent modules that map a model specification and its observations to the parameters of a variational posterior.
